Leukoplakia

A four-case series reports smaller lesions after treatment, while the randomized trial reports less pain after cryosurgery. A mapped mouse study found no lesion-characteristic effect.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A four-case series reports smaller lesions after treatment, while the randomized trial reports less pain after cryosurgery. A mapped mouse study found no lesion-characteristic effect.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Oral > Leukoplakia category contains two human publications: a four-case series and an 18-participant randomized trial of LLLT after cryosurgery. One mouse study explicitly examining oral leukoplakia is cross-indexed under Oncology > Tumor growth and is mapped as related preclinical evidence.

Human and clinical evidence

The case series reported reduced mean lesion area after at least 10 treatments, without a control group. The randomized study reported less pain after cryosurgery; it does not establish PBM monotherapy as a lesion treatment or cancer-prevention strategy (Jagtap et al. 2018; Ribeiro et al. 2011). Neither human report tests malignant transformation, recurrence, or long-term lesion control. Reduced area in four cases and post-cryosurgery analgesia are different outcomes. Given the potentially premalignant nature of leukoplakia, PBM should not be inferred to replace biopsy, risk-factor modification, surveillance, or definitive treatment.

Primary original studies: Jagtap et al. 2018 Ribeiro et al. 2011

Animal evidence

In a 4-NQO mouse model, PBM did not alter the clinical or histological characteristics of induced oral leukoplakia or carcinoma (Neculqueo et al., 2022).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Jagtap et al. report 660 nm visible red light over at least 10 sessions. Ribeiro et al. used 660 nm light at 49 J/cm² for 94 seconds, with 3 treatments over 4 days after cryosurgery. These regimens answer different questions: lesion-area change versus post-procedure pain. They do not establish a PBM-only leukoplakia treatment.

Interpretation

Leukoplakia can be premalignant, so lesion-area change or pain relief should not be interpreted as cancer prevention. The randomized study tested PBM after cryosurgery, while the lesion-size series lacked a control. These findings do not replace biopsy, surveillance, risk-factor care, or established lesion management.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. A small series reports lesion shrinkage, while the trial concerns pain after cryosurgery.
Publications and records3 unique titles: 2 exact-category human reports and 1 mapped mouse study.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The human evidence includes a four-case series measuring lesion area and a randomized study of pain after cryosurgery. These are different outcomes, and neither establishes PBM monotherapy as a treatment to prevent malignant transformation. A mapped mouse study found no change in lesion or tumor characteristics.
